newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-M3 review easier after target zone hit.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-M3 review easier after target zone hit.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday the fact June M3 money supply growth had come within the central bank's target corridor would make the bank's review of the indicator this week easier.

"It is comforting to see that M3 has reached the target corridor. It means that our discussion about M3 (as an indicator for monetary policy) will be easier," Welteke told reporters before an event in Frankfurt.
Asked whether he thought M3 growth would remain in the 3.5 to 6.5 percent corridor, Welteke said: "That is difficult to say."
M3 money supply growth fell to 6.4 percent in June from 7.0 percent in May, reaching the central bank's target zone for the first time this year.
The Bundesbank, which uses M3 as a leading indicator for inflation when setting interest rates, will review the indicator at its regular council meeting on Thursday.
Analysts do not expect any change to the 3.5 to 6.5 percent 1997 target zone.
